context.body: Saul heard that David was discovered, with the men who were with him. Now Saul was sitting in Gibeah, under the tamarisk tree in Ramah, with his spear in his hand….
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Saul accuses his servants, Doeg reports Ahimelech, the priests are condemned, and Abiathar escapes to David, who receives responsibility for the danger.
observations.label: Nob bears the cost of Saul’s suspicion: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps Saul, Doeg, Ahimelech, the priests, Abiathar, and David, Gibeah, Nob, and David’s refuge, accusing, reporting, questioning, killing, escaping, confessing, and promising protection visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: Nob bears the cost of Saul’s suspicion: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: Saul, Doeg, Ahimelech, the priests, Abiathar, and David · Gibeah, Nob, and David’s refuge · accusing, reporting, questioning, killing, escaping, confessing, and promising protection · the pursuit of David destroys the priestly city and binds Abiathar to him
observations.label: Relationships named in 1 Samuel 22:6–23

payload.posture: Read 1 Samuel 22:6–23 as its own flight, covenant, and restraint David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places the pursuit of David destroys the priestly city and binds Abiathar to him inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
payload.title: Nob bears the cost of Saul’s suspicion
